subject.title: Bug: async sessions_send results are not delivered cleanly to Telegram-bound requester session

question: Should asynchronous `sessions_send` completion delivery always produce one clean requester-channel result, with all ping-pong and wrapper events kept internal, or should any requester-facing continuation remain agent-controlled?
rationale: The open reverse-call guard addresses only one duplication source; deciding the durable external-delivery semantics determines whether the remaining work is a narrow bug fix or a broader A2A contract change.

options.title: Adopt exactly-once requester delivery
options.body: Treat async A2A completion as one clean delivery to the requester’s preserved channel context and suppress internal wrapper/continuation traffic from external channels.

options.title: Keep agent-controlled continuation
options.body: Retain the current announce/continuation model and document that user-visible delivery may require the requester agent to decide how to relay results.

options.title: Separate delivery modes
options.body: Preserve current behavior by default while adding an explicit future A2A mode for deterministic requester-channel delivery after a design review.

recommendation.title: Adopt exactly-once requester delivery
recommendation.body: Treat async A2A completion as one clean delivery to the requester’s preserved channel context and suppress internal wrapper/continuation traffic from external channels.

likelyOwner.reason: Feature-history evidence and the explicit request for A2A contract clarification point to this ownership path.
